title: Type 2 Diabetes Overview
content: Type 2 diabetes often develops gradually. Common symptoms include increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision, and slow-healing sores. Hemoglobin A1c is commonly used for diagnosis and monitoring over the prior two to three months.

title: High Blood Pressure Risk Factors
content: High blood pressure risk increases with older age, obesity, high salt intake, low physical activity, diabetes, kidney disease, and family history. Lifestyle changes such as exercise, weight reduction, and lower sodium intake are important first-line measures.

title: Pneumonia Symptoms and Care
content: Pneumonia may cause cough, fever, chills, chest discomfort, rapid breathing, and shortness of breath. Older adults can have atypical symptoms. Severe breathing difficulty, confusion, or low oxygen are warning signs that need urgent assessment.

title: Heart Failure Symptoms
content: Heart failure can cause shortness of breath, fatigue, ankle swelling, and exercise intolerance. Fluid retention and worsening breathing when lying flat are common. Management usually combines medication, sodium control, and monitoring for decompensation.

title: COPD Care Principles
content: COPD commonly presents with chronic cough, sputum production, and exertional dyspnea. Smoking cessation, inhaled therapy, vaccination, and pulmonary rehabilitation are key components of long-term management.
